focus: pre-ClayOS authenticated release metadata and rollback semantics
primary_evidence_basis: The Update Framework model starts from trusted root metadata/keys provisioned to the client and uses monotonic metadata versions to detect rollback.
DSSE authenticates payload type plus payload bytes through pre-authentication encoding and recommends signature verification before trusting parsed payload semantics.
in-toto Statement/v1 provides typed subject digests suitable for binding exact ClayEnv manifest and ClayVM artifact identities.
Ed25519 verification is delegated to the pinned cryptography library rather than implemented as project-specific cryptography.
candidate_mechanism: Verify an externally pinned 32-byte Ed25519 public-key object before using it.
Verify a DSSE envelope before parsing its in-toto Statement/v1 payload.
Bind signed subjects to the exact ClayEnvManifest/v1 and ClayVMArtifact/v1 bytes and bind vm_blob_sha256 across signed predicate and existing provenance manifest.
Execute only through the existing run_artifact -> ClayOS.exec_artifact path.
Persist a canonical release state under an exclusive file lock; reject lower signed releaseVersion and same-version/different-payload equivocation.
Fail closed on a changed trusted key after state exists until a separate root-rotation protocol is defined.
ordinary_regressions: valid signed release executes and exact replay remains idempotent
trusted-key file substitution rejected against supplied key pin
different valid artifact/manifest pair rejected under another signed release
lower signed release version rejected after newer release
same release version with different signed payload rejected as equivocation
root-key change rejected until rotation protocol exists

grf.generated_reality: A DSSE signature plus a hash-pinned Ed25519 public key supplied to release-run constitutes independent release authority.
grf.strongest_counter_reality: If the same invoking principal can select both the public-key path and its expected hash, the verifier proves consistency with a chosen key but cannot prove that the key came from an independently authorized trust root.
grf.observed_counterevidence: PR 651 public CLI currently accepts both --trusted-release-key and --trusted-release-key-sha256. Therefore the root origin is an external assumption, not enforced authority inside this public surface.
grf.second_counter_reality: Monotonic local release state detects stale metadata while intact but can itself be rolled back by host/snapshot restoration unless anchored in a stronger non-rollbackable or externally reconciled state.

promotion_blockers: Source the accepted release root from a non-caller-controlled OS/deployment trust boundary or equivalent canonical trust store.
Prove arbitrary caller-selected root substitution cannot authorize release execution.
Define root-key rotation and recovery rather than silently accepting a new key.
Define rollback-resistant or externally reconciled release-version state and test host/snapshot rollback.
Compose canonical package/module closure identity into signed release subjects once CM-07 package resolution is canonical.
Rebase/retest the release candidate against current product main after concurrent ClayEnv/package changes.

coordination.parallel_package_front: PR 650 canonical package identity remains a separate current candidate and may overlap clayenv CLI/workflow files.
coordination.parallel_import_mode_front: PR 635 preserves MODULE versus WILDCARD metadata but remains non-linking.
coordination.survivor_rule: Do not overwrite or merge stale overlapping ClayEnv candidates without fresh-main recomposition and exact-head retest.
